events.what: Watt with three AI co-authors reports a failed campaign to prove the mass gap; constructs a mass-gapped noncommutative 4D gauge theory and argues the question 'dissolves' by recontextualisation
events.credibility_reason: Self-published Zenodo report, no expert uptake; by its own account it failed to prove the continuum mass gap and hit a factor-of-23 lattice/continuum discrepancy.
events.ai_basis: using adversarial AI collaboration across three frontier models

events.what: Silva-Filho's Lean-4 'certified' Unconditional Trilogy claiming a full proof
events.credibility_reason: Landmark Millennium problem; self-published on Zenodo amid a flood of crank claims; no expert uptake; Clay and Wikipedia still list it unsolved; relies only on the author's own Lean repository (F10) whose statement nobody has compared with the Clay formulation.
Self-published on a landmark problem, no uptake, Clay page still lists unsolved; method outside rigorous constructive QFT.

events.what: Agawa's SU(N) mass gap proof preprint, retracted by the author
Jacobsen's constructive SU(3) proof claim on arXiv, withdrawn by arXiv administrators
events.credibility_reason: Withdrawn by arXiv administrators for failing content-quality standards.

judgement.doubts: The Watt/AI report is kept in the record as evidence of an AI attempt, but it settles only changed questions (noncommutative theory, reframing) and cannot set a status. Many further self-published claims were not opened; none shows any expert uptake.

corrections.why: F3/F5: the record's own summary says the Watt report 'failed to prove the continuum mass gap' and 'reframed rather than solved the problem'. Its constructions (a noncommutative gauge theory) are a variant, not a bound on this bullet. The other claims were retracted, withdrawn, or are not credible. Nothing survives step 1, and nothing was resolved before the snapshot.
other: no event survives for the status to rest on, so no AI role applies. The Watt AI campaign stays in the record as evidence.
